unanticipated_findings: REPLAY WITHIN THE FRESHNESS WINDOW IS POSSIBLE: the X-Webhook-Delivery header is the deduplication key (service.py:116) but is NOT covered by the signature (signature.py:32-45 signs only timestamp + body). An attacker who captures one signed delivery can resend the identical body/timestamp/signature with a mutated delivery id and it is accepted as new work, unlimited times, for the whole 300s tolerance window. Reproduced against the running server: one signed body {"event":"payout","amt":9999} posted with X-Webhook-Delivery values 'real-1', 'real-1', 'attacker-forged-2', 'attacker-forged-3' returned 202, 200(duplicate), 202, 202 — three payout events written to events.jsonl from a single signed request. Ironically the fallback path is safe: when the header is absent, the key is sha256(body), which the signature does cover (service.py:114-115). Fix would be to include the delivery id in the canonical message, or to key dedup on (sender, timestamp, sha256(body)) when the header is unsigned.

DEAD-LETTERED DELIVERIES ARE PERMANENTLY UNRECOVERABLE VIA THE SENDER: store.record's ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (store.py:171) ignores the existing row's status, so once a delivery reaches DEAD, any subsequent resend of that same delivery id gets 200 'duplicate' and is dropped. Reproduced directly: after 5 failing dispatches the row is `dead attempts 5`, and re-calling service.receive with the same valid signature/id printed `sender resend after dead-letter: 200 duplicate`. The sender is told everything is fine while the event is permanently lost, and the only recovery is manual DB surgery — there is no requeue command and the README roadmap (line 235) only lists a retention policy as future work.

ALL SQLITE I/O RUNS SYNCHRONOUSLY ON THE ASYNCIO EVENT LOOP: service.receive is `async def` but calls the blocking sqlite3 API directly (service.py:122 store.record, app.py:153 store.counts), with no asyncio.to_thread. Combined with `PRAGMA synchronous = FULL` (store.py:121), every accepted delivery performs an fsync on the event loop thread, stalling every other in-flight request and the recovery loop for its duration. The p99 test (tests/e2e/test_resposta_rapida.py:99-121) is strictly sequential, so it cannot detect this; a concurrent load test on a slow disk would. The handler itself is correctly offloaded (handlers.py:86 uses asyncio.to_thread) — only the store is not.

README HAS THREE TRUNCATED SENTENCES AND ONE DANGLING CROSS-REFERENCE, shipped as-is: README.md:7-8 'a suíte segundos' is missing its verb and number; README.md:183-184 'A superfície completa, com todos os estados e o texto exato das mensagens, está' ends mid-sentence and points at a full-surface document that does not exist in the repo; README.md:253-254 'Mudanças que alterem verificação de assinatura, deduplicação ou o contrato do' ends mid-word. The same truncation appears in source: src/webhook_receiver/cli.py:4 begins mid-sentence with 'governam tudo aqui:' (the subject of the sentence is gone).

NO EXAMPLE CONFIG FILE IS SHIPPED. `webhook-receiver check` defaults to ./webhook-receiver.toml (cli.py:42) but the repo contains no such file and no .example/.sample variant, so the bare command in a clean checkout fails until the operator hand-transcribes the TOML out of README.md:99-107. The error path is good (it prints the format), but a committed sample file is the norm here and its absence is the one place the documentation-to-working-service path required me to author a file rather than copy one.

store.mark_handled(row_id, now) accepts a `now` parameter and never uses it (store.py:229-238) — the UPDATE binds only status and row_id. Callers (service.py:169) pass self.clock() believing a timestamp is recorded; nothing is. Harmless today but it means a handled delivery carries no completion time, and `received_at` is the only temporal record.

The 413 path returns without draining the request body: app.py:70-71 returns None as soon as the byte count exceeds 1 MiB, mid-`request.stream()`. With HTTP keep-alive and a large upload, abandoning the unread body can leave the connection in an indeterminate state for the client. The test at tests/e2e/test_http.py:167-171 uses ASGITransport, which buffers the whole body in memory first and therefore cannot exercise this.

Test package layout is inconsistent: tests/__init__.py and tests/e2e/__init__.py exist, but tests/unit/ and tests/integration/ have no __init__.py. Collection currently works via rootdir insertion, but the asymmetry is a latent basename-collision hazard if two test modules in different unpackaged directories ever share a name.
